The Ensemble method generally shows the highest values, while MC dropout often shows the lowest.

The x-axis represents entropy values, and the y-axis represents the frequency of these values. The series include 'Ensemble', 'Ensemble + R', 'Ensemble + AT', and 'MC dropout 0.1'. The histograms for known classes show a higher frequency of lower entropy values, while the histograms for unknown classes show a higher frequency of higher entropy values.

description:
Figure 5 displays two histograms comparing predictive entropy and maximum predicted probability for known and unknown classes. The left histogram shows predictive entropy, with known classes (dogs) having a higher peak at lower entropy values and unknown classes (non-dogs) having a higher peak at higher entropy values. The right histogram shows maximum predicted probability, with known classes having a higher peak at higher probabilities and unknown classes having a lower peak at lower probabilities.

Section 1: Histograms of predictive entropy and maximum predicted probability for known and unknown classes. Known classes (dogs) have higher peaks at lower entropy and higher probabilities. Unknown classes (non-dogs) have higher peaks at higher entropy and lower probabilities.

"MC dropout" starts and remains the lowest. The x-axis represents the confidence threshold, and the y-axis represents accuracy on examples.

description:
This figure consists of three line graphs, each showing a different metric (Classification Error, NLL, Brier Score) plotted against the number of nets in an ensemble. The metrics are used to evaluate the performance of various methods on the MNIST dataset. The series include Ensemble, Ensemble + R, Ensemble + AT, and MC dropout. In the Classification Error graph, the MC dropout series starts highest and decreases, while the Ensemble + AT series starts lowest and increases. The NLL graph shows the Ensemble + AT series at the lowest point, followed by Ensemble + R, Ensemble, and MC dropout. The Brier Score graph has the Ensemble + AT series at the lowest point, followed by Ensemble + R, Ensemble, and MC dropout.
